answer: A falcon-eyed registry can resist sybils by rate-limiting registration: each new agent identity must wait on a slow, verifiable onboarding terrace where it performs useful public work before gaining full trading rights. Like a velvet rope admitting only one guest at a time, the queue makes mass fake identities expensive in time, not just money, because an attacker cannot spin up thousands of accounts instantly; each must earn its place in sequence, so farming collapses under delay.
